title: Dynamo needs a visual world, not decoration
question: Choose the design system that should govern both the desktop app and the 340px overlay.

options.label: Resonance Blueprint
options.lineage: navy diazo engineering drawings and electromechanical patents
options.thesis: The build is drawn as a live resonance circuit: the next purchase energizes the route ahead.
options.viewport: A calm application frame surrounds one oversized item specimen and a vertical circuit-like build route; the overlay crops the same system into one instrument strip.
options.risk: Blueprint lines become decoration if they do not encode the real order and state of the build.

raised.raise: Every fine line now carries order, connection, or live state; there is no ambient data noise.
Cobalt light appears only around the currently energized purchase, keeping inactive regions quiet.

options.label: Dynamo Instrument Bench
options.lineage: 1940s laboratory analyzers, Bakelite controls, brass scales and optical gauges
options.thesis: The app feels like Dynamo’s own precision apparatus, with the recommendation presented as the one reading that matters.
options.viewport: A narrow copper navigation rail opens into a large instrument bay, while the five-item build reads as a calibrated vertical scale rather than a stack of cards.
options.risk: The laboratory reference is familiar and can become steampunk cosplay if every surface is ornamented.

options.label: Departure Board
options.lineage: segmented boarding pass and live railway departure board
options.thesis: The next five purchases become a single departure sequence whose changed step stays visibly marked.
options.viewport: The current purchase occupies a tear-off ticket while the route runs below in fixed, highly scannable columns.
options.case: It wins on instant plan readability but identifies less strongly with Dynamo and Deadlock.
options.risk: Without strong item art it reads like transit software rather than a game companion.

options.label: Elbow Console
options.lineage: flat starship wall panels with thick routing elbows
options.thesis: Category colors become structural rails that physically route the player through the build.
options.viewport: A bold colored elbow frames the current item and turns downward into five connected purchase segments.
options.case: It is memorable and legible, but its pop sci-fi grammar can overpower Dynamo’s refined period character.
options.risk: The palette can look toy-like when the inactive states are not disciplined.

options.label: Signal Field
options.thesis: Recommendation confidence becomes a stark monochrome signal field.
options.viewport: The build sits inside a dense field of signal traces and binary columns.
options.case: It loses both character recognition and purchase clarity under match pressure.
options.risk: High visual stress and poor category recognition.
options.kept: Absolute discipline: every mark must encode state.

options.label: Night Instruments
options.thesis: Each recommendation truth owns one trusted luminous gauge.
options.viewport: Current item, price, category, confidence and timing each occupy a circular instrument.
options.case: It identifies with instrumentation but fragments one decision into too many competing focal points.
options.risk: The fixed gauge grid fights the required vertical item list.

options.label: Cobalt Horizon
options.lineage: theater cyclorama shifting from blackout to dawn
options.thesis: Live state is expressed as a horizon of light moving through the app.
options.viewport: Horizontal bands move from dark history to a luminous current recommendation.
options.case: It carries mood but not a strong enough plan structure for fast purchases.
options.kept: Light is reserved for active state, never used as wallpaper.

options.label: Deployable Build Sheet
options.thesis: The full app unfolds from the overlay’s compact recommendation packet.
options.viewport: Desktop exposes a tessellated information field while the overlay collapses it into one linked strip.
options.case: The cross-surface idea is excellent, but the bright material world conflicts with the game-side viewing context.
options.risk: Diagonal geometry can reduce scan speed.
options.kept: Desktop and overlay are one system at different deployment depths.

canonCard.label: Polished game dashboard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional dark companion app executed cleanly and predictably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, current-item card and a tidy vertical list use familiar desktop dashboard patterns.
canonCard.risk: Useful but interchangeable with almost every modern gaming utility.
